title: Père Hacki (Jesuit agent in Poland) → Queen Christina of Sweden, c. 18 ciphered letters on the Polish election
correspondents: Père Hacki → Christine de Suède
place: Warsaw, Thorn, Danzig, Breslau, Kalisz, Petricovie

folio_note: each a short autograph sheet 'Lettre chiffrée sur les affaires de Pologne' (ff. 312-352); no. 228 (Petricovie, 28 Feb 1669) has the figures glossed above each group by another hand
status: Catalogue: 'Lettre chiffrée sur les affaires de Pologne'. Eight neighbouring sheets are 'Mise en clair d'une dépêche chiffrée' (nos. 237-239, 242, 244, 245, 249, 253), i.e. clear versions of Hacki's own cipher letters, plus the glossed no. 228: the key can be rebuilt from them. No decipherment of the ciphered sheets themselves is noted. Not on DECODE (known.py, 28 Oct 2026). Checked 28 Oct 2026: 28 Oct 2026 verify: Calames confirms no. 234 (16 Nov 1668) as 'Lettre chiffrée sur les affaires de Pologne'; no images online, no published decipherment found. III (Amsterdam 1759), section on the Polish election (pp. ~340-390): extracts and paraphrases of Père Prieur Hacki's despatches and Christina's instruction to him, from 'Negoziati di Polonia'; the dated Hacki letters (31 Oct 1668-19 Apr 1669) are not printed in full Arckenholtz notes that he holds Christina's ciphers (four kinds, from Rome) and that some of her ciphered letters are undeciphered in print. why: Christina's own campaign for the Polish crown in 1668-69 (Jean Casimir's abdication), told by her agent in cipher.
